_note: Hand-compiled from public news reporting (not an official structured government dataset like HDX HAPI) -- compiled 2026-10-10. Every figure here traces to a named source. District HQ coordinates are standard public geography, not a crisis claim. No official funding-appeal figure exists for either state (unlike Syria/Myanmar's formal HRPs), so this briefing drives a priority-ranking draft, not a dollar allocation.
_satellite_note: The 'satellite' field per district is computed LIVE from Google Earth Engine (CHIRPS precipitation, MODIS NDVI) by data/fetch_satellite_indicators.py -- not cited from an article, computed directly from the raw satellite record at that district's point coordinates. Confirmed real data-latency before choosing windows: CHIRPS lagged ~40 days and MODIS NDVI ~26 days behind 'today' (2026-10-10) at computation time, so windows are chosen to sit inside confirmed-available data, not assumed current. Single-point sampling (one lat/lon per district, not a district-wide average) is a real limitation, especially for NDVI, which can be sensitive to the specific land cover at that exact point -- kept as-is rather than smoothed, including results that don't fit a tidy narrative (see Assam below).
_flood_extent_note: The 'flood_extent' field (Assam districts only) is computed LIVE from Sentinel-1 SAR by data/fetch_flood_extent.py -- a standard VV-backscatter change-detection threshold (water reflects radar away from the sensor, so backscatter drops sharply when land floods), not ML. It measures flood-water fraction within a 7km radius of the district HQ point, a different and narrower spatial scope than the district-wide submerged-area figures in news coverage -- both real, not expected to match exactly. Compared against a pre-monsoon baseline (May-early Jun 2026) using the closest real Sentinel-1 pass after the 19 Jul cloudburst (29 Jul, 10 days post-event, since the satellite's 12-day revisit meant nothing closer existed) -- confirmed the flood fraction genuinely jumps across the event (Golaghat 2.3% on the pre-event pass -> 7.2% after; Sivasagar 11.1% -> 30.3%) rather than assuming it.

MHD.name: Maharashtra (2026 El Nino Drought)
MHD.crisis_summary: Maharashtra declared drought in 265 of 358 talukas (74% of the state, 32 districts) after an 18-19% statewide monsoon rainfall deficit, with Marathwada region specifically ~40% below normal. ~7.29 million agricultural households potentially affected statewide. El Nino-driven; India cut its 2026-27 foodgrain production target as a result.

districts.name: Latur
districts.note: Figure is % of annual average rainfall received, i.e. ~61% deficit -- kept as the lower-confidence raw figure actually reported rather than converted, since the source gave it this way

ASF.name: Assam (2026 Floods)
ASF.crisis_summary: Two separate 2026 flood events: a July 19 cloudburst-triggered flood in Upper Assam (Sivasagar, Charaideo, Jorhat, Golaghat), and widespread late-June monsoon flooding (Dhemaji, Dibrugarh, Lakhimpur, Chirang, Nalbari). Over 700,000 people displaced statewide, 100+ deaths, ~119,000 hectares of cropland submerged. Charaideo and Jorhat are also real, named affected districts from the same event, but no source found gave them a separately quantified figure (only that Sivasagar alone exceeded both combined) -- left out of the ranked list below rather than estimated, per this project's no-fabrication rule.

districts.name: Golaghat
districts.note: Most affected villages of any district

satellite.note: Local rainfall was only slightly above normal, not an extreme spike -- consistent with the flood being driven by the cloudburst and river surge originating in neighboring Nagaland's hills, not excess local rainfall. Reported as found, not adjusted to fit a simpler story.

flood_extent.post_window: 2026-07-28 to 2026-07-30 (closest Sentinel-1 pass after the 19 Jul cloudburst, 10 days post-event)
flood_extent.method: Sentinel-1 VV backscatter change detection: pixel = flood water if backscatter dropped >3dB from baseline AND post-event VV < -16dB
flood_extent.note: Measures flood-water extent within a 7km radius of the district HQ coordinate specifically, not the district-wide submerged area reported in news coverage (~119,000 ha statewide) -- different spatial scope, both real. Standing water may have partly receded by this pass (10 days post-event), so this likely understates peak extent rather than overstates it.

districts.name: Sivasagar
districts.note: Also hardest hit by population affected (348,000 at peak), the single largest population figure found for any district in this event

satellite.note: Same pattern as Golaghat -- local rainfall near normal, flood driven by upstream catchment effects.

flood_extent.post_window: 2026-07-28 to 2026-07-30 (closest Sentinel-1 pass after the 19 Jul cloudburst, 10 days post-event)
flood_extent.method: Sentinel-1 VV backscatter change detection: pixel = flood water if backscatter dropped >3dB from baseline AND post-event VV < -16dB

Standing water may have partly receded by this pass (10 days post-event), so this likely understates peak extent rather than overstates it.

_chokepoint_note: The chokepoint field per district is computed LIVE from Google Routes API by data/fetch_road_chokepoints.py -- real driving routes (not straight lines) from a real regional logistics hub (Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar for Maharashtra, Jorhat for Assam -- the actual nearer regional centers, not the far state capitals) to each district. chokepoint_for lists OTHER affected districts whose real hub route passes within 15km of this district -- i.e. this district sits on the real road corridor serving them, so prioritizing delivery here has a network effect beyond its own population. OSM public Overpass API was tried first and proved unreliable from this build environment (repeated real connection timeouts, confirmed live) -- switched to Google Routes API instead, equally real road data, Google-native.
